statement: Let cnt(v) be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] = v. The function returns a result r, and r = 0 if there is no integer v such that cnt(v) > 0 and cnt(v+1) > 0; otherwise r = max { cnt(v) + cnt(v+1) | v is an integer, cnt(v) > 0, cnt(v+1) > 0 }.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 20000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: The function returns a result r, and 0 <= r <= len(nums).
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 20000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: The function returns a result r; no arithmetic overflow, out-of-bounds access, or panic occurs.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 20000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: The function returns a result r, and either r = 0 or r >= 2.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 20000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: The function returns a result r, and r = len(nums) if and only if there exists an integer a such that (1) for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), nums[i] = a or nums[i] = a+1, and (2) there is at least one index i with nums[i] = a and at least one index j with nums[j] = a+1.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 20000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Let cnt(v) be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] = v. The function returns a result r. If r > 0, then there exists an integer v such that cnt(v) > 0, cnt(v+1) > 0, and r = cnt(v) + cnt(v+1).
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 20000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Let cnt(v) be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] = v. The function returns a result r, and for every integer v with cnt(v) > 0 and cnt(v+1) > 0, cnt(v) + cnt(v+1) <= r.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 20000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: For any slice nums' satisfying the stated preconditions, if for every integer v the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] = v equals the number of indices j with 0 <= j < len(nums') and nums'[j] = v, then the function returns a result r on nums and a result r' on nums', and r = r'.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 20000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; and 1 <= len(nums') <= 20000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums'), -1000000000 <= nums'[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Let nums' be the slice obtained by appending x to nums, so len(nums') = len(nums) + 1, nums'[i] = nums[i] for 0 <= i < len(nums), and nums'[len(nums)] = x. The function returns a result r on nums and a result r' on nums', and r' >= r.

The function returns a result r. If r > 0, then there exist indices 0 <= i_0 < i_1 < ... < i_{r-1} < len(nums) such that the difference between the maximum and minimum of the values nums[i_0], ..., nums[i_{r-1}] is exactly 1.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 20000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Let cnt(v) be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] = v, and let M be the maximum of cnt(v) over all integers v with cnt(v) > 0 (well-defined because len(nums) >= 1). The function returns a result r, and r <= 2 * M.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 20000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: A harmonious subsequence of nums is a sequence nums[i_0], ..., nums[i_{k-1}] for indices 0 <= i_0 < ... < i_{k-1} < len(nums) with k >= 2 and max(nums[i_0], ..., nums[i_{k-1}]) - min(nums[i_0], ..., nums[i_{k-1}]) = 1. The function returns a result r, and for every harmonious subsequence of nums of length k, k <= r.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 20000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.
